title: Intellectual property
competency: Recognize the basics of intellectual property rights and distinguish trade secrets, patents, copyrights and trademarks.

keywords.def: A range of intangible rights of ownership of an asset such as a software program or designed information system.
Confidential business information that gives a competitive advantage; it may be sold or licensed.
An exclusive, limited-duration right granted for an invention that is new, non-obvious and useful; its technical details are published.
Protection of original works of authorship such as literary works, music, art and software; it is automatic.
A sign, word or symbol that distinguishes the goods or services of one enterprise from those of others.

ideas.name: Intellectual property rights and trade secrets

en.text: Intellectual property rights are intangible rights of ownership of an asset such as a software program or a designed information system. Ethiopia's Proclamation No. 320 of 2003 defines intellectual property as a legal right over a creative work of the human intellect. Four types matter for software: trade secrets, patents, copyrights and trademarks. A trade secret is confidential information that may be sold or licensed, such as customer lists, source code or a drink recipe.

ideas.name: Patents and the Ethiopian Intellectual Property Authority

en.text: A patent is an exclusive right granted for an invention: the owner decides how, or whether, others may use it, and in exchange publishes its technical details. Others may not make, use or sell it. Examples include the light bulb, the telephone, Bluetooth, Google's PageRank algorithm and Amazon's 1-Click ordering. Not all software can be patented: in Ethiopia the Ethiopian Intellectual Property Authority (EIPA) requires an invention to be new, to involve an inventive step and to be capable of industrial application.

en.text: Copyright protects original works of authorship, such as literary works, music, art, computer software, architecture and graphical user interfaces. It is automatic once you create the work, but you must register it to file a lawsuit. A trademark is a sign that distinguishes the goods or services of one enterprise from others, such as the Ride, Microsoft and Meta logos. Patents and copyrights expire, but trademark rights come from use and can last indefinitely.

screens.title: Copyrights

notes.text: p.15 lists "Airbnb, Amazon, One-click" as patented software. Airbnb and Amazon are companies; the well-known patents are Amazon's 1-Click ordering method and Google's PageRank algorithm (both now expired). The lesson uses this corrected wording.

The text says "Ethiopian Intellectual Property Office" while Figure 1.16 and Activity 1.5 say "Authority". It was set up as the Office in 2003 and is now the Ethiopian Intellectual Property Authority (EIPA, eipo.gov.et). The lesson uses EIPA.

p.16 says "many companies in our country with registered trademarks. Examples are Ride, Meta, and Microsoft." Only Ride is Ethiopian. Local examples could be Ethio telecom, Ethiopian Airlines or Commercial Bank of Ethiopia.

The rules "trademark registration is not required" and "copyright registration is needed to sue" follow US practice. Under Ethiopian law (Trademark Proclamation No. 501 of 2006, Copyright Proclamation No. 410 of 2004) trademark rights generally come from registration with EIPA. Teacher please check before teaching these as Ethiopian rules.

Proclamation numbers are written "No. 320 of 2003" instead of a slash so the player does not show them as fractions. The patent application steps are added from the Activity 1.5 Q2 model answer; the 20-year patent term is not in the book and is not taught.
